sun.purpose: The low sun on the water. The only warm value in the system: primary action, checked checkbox, playing track, meter fill, caret, selection wash and focus ring. Measured at 0.41% frame coverage.

sun-ink.purpose: Near-black ink on brass fills only. 7.56:1 on --sun.

line.purpose: The 1px waterline and the pending band's hatch. A rule, never an accent, never text.

ok.purpose: The 7px connection dot when a watch is present. Never text.

alert.purpose: Untagged-file warning, over-capacity readout, failure notice tag. 5.06:1 on --air, 4.77:1 on --notice-ground, 4.74:1 on the .07 tint, 5.08:1 on --d3. Always paired with a word. Fourth use: the delete control and its confirmation, the only irreversible action in the app. Allowed only on opaque grounds — --d3 5.08:1, --notice-ground 4.77:1 — and forbidden on a wall row, where it is 3.80:1 selected and 4.12:1 hovered.

ground.purpose: The body behind the app; visible only at the window's own edges.

air.purpose: The surface above the waterline: the app field and the titlebar.

air-2.purpose: Top stop of the sources rail gradient; the rail's flat ground at <=1020px.

d1.purpose: The lit surface of the water. The lightest ground below the line, and the one that rises behind the wall head, list and capacity as the watch fills.

d2.purpose: Bottom stop of the watch wall's own gradient.

d3.purpose: Top stop of the wall gradient, mid stop of the water, and the opaque backing under the capacity readout.

d4.purpose: The floor of the water and the ground of the player bar. The deepest surface on screen.

notice-ground.purpose: Opaque ground for the transfer failure headline: --air with the alert hue flattened in. Exists so --alert's 4.77:1 is a property of the rule and not of the three layers behind it.

ink.purpose: Titles, primary text, the seek thumb. 14.99:1 on --air; never below 12.38:1 anywhere in the app.

ink-dim.purpose: Secondary lines, and the required ink on every composite ground where --ink-faint fails: rail counts, wall head, wall list. 6.38:1 on --air, 5.27:1 on --d1.

ink-faint.purpose: The quietest legible tier: wordmark, rail heads, formats, timecodes, connection status. 5.28:1 on --air, 4.93:1 at its worst shipped ground (the transfer card over bright artwork). Was #5a6875 = 3.18:1.

surface.purpose: Hover raise. Also the checkbox and seek rest ground.

surface-2.purpose: Current/rest raise: secondary buttons, the current nav item, play/pause, the meter track.

hairline.purpose: The edge of something you can press.

hairline-2.purpose: Every structural divider and panel edge in the app.

edge.purpose: Control boundaries only — checkbox and button edges. Not a hairline and not a replacement for one: the same rgba(226,236,247,x) veil family, a new alpha rather than a new hue. Measured 3.40 on --air, 3.37 --air-2, 3.23 --d1, 3.34 --d2, 3.40 --d3, 3.37 --d4, 3.39 --notice-ground, 3.23 hovered wall row, 3.16 selected wall row. Worst case 3.16:1, over 1.4.11's 3:1. --hairline is 1.25-1.35:1 on the same grounds and identifies nothing. Disabled controls keep --hairline deliberately.

display.purpose: The album hero title. One line, clipped with an ellipsis at desktop; wraps at <=720px. Measured cap height 18.4px app-pixels.

headline.purpose: The free-space number on the watch wall. The largest text in the app on purpose, because capacity governs every decision. Tabular numerals.

title.purpose: Panel headings and empty-state heads (14px); the transfer card's heading at 13.5px.

body.purpose: The default. Track titles, album credits, the disconnected explanation.

dense.purpose: The watch wall list (12px), nav items and player now-playing (12.5px), button faces (12.5px / 590).

detail.purpose: Sub-lines and metadata: durations, sizes, hero facts, timecodes, hints, notice bodies.

label.purpose: Uppercase 0.14em tracking: the wordmark, rail section heads, the player format badge. Notice and pre-warning tags use 0.1em at weight 640.

shadows.name: cover-lift
shadows.purpose: The 132px hero album cover only. The single true drop shadow in the app; it is the one object presented as a physical thing.

shadows.name: frame-highlight
shadows.purpose: A 1px top light on every cover frame at every size (.06 on the hero cover). Joinery, not elevation.

shadows.name: waterline-bloom
shadows.purpose: The glow under the 1px waterline, and the only luminous object in the app. Directional by necessity: offset 6px down with a -4px spread so the light falls into the water. A symmetrical halo washed the ground the wall list scrolls across and pushed those rows under AA.

shadows.name: glass-transfer
shadows.purpose: The one floating surface. The near-opaque base under the blur is load-bearing: the card floats over scrolling album art, and with a 4.8% veil its inks inherited whatever was behind them (3.99:1 on the failure headline over bright art).

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: The only easing curve in the system.

motion.name: t-quick
motion.purpose: Linear background, colour and opacity on every interactive element.

motion.name: t-settle
motion.purpose: State arrivals: the transfer card's @starting-style entry, the meter's scaleX, the pending band's opacity, the sink keyframe.

motion.name: t-tide
motion.purpose: The water's translateY. The only slow thing in the app, and it runs once per transfer.

breakpoints.name: narrow
breakpoints.note: One column. The gauge drops from 132px to 84px (set on `.wall`, because a container query cannot reach `:root`) and nothing else about the water changes. This was previously a distinct behaviour — a fixed band with `transform: none` — and is now the same mechanism at a different height.

radiusExceptions.where: the 3px seek track and the 3px transfer meter
radiusExceptions.why: A 6px radius on a 3px-tall bar is a pill, not a corner.
The ring hugs arbitrary geometry; it takes the smallest radius that stops the corners reading as cut.

radiusExceptions.where: the 15px checkbox and the icon buttons
radiusExceptions.why: Below the scale's floor of roughly 16px in the short dimension.

radiusExceptions.where: the scrollbar thumb (9px wide) and the base cover frame
radiusExceptions.why: Half the thumb's own width; the cover family scales 5px -> 8px so its corner reads constant.

components.name: Watch Wall with Waterline
components.description: The app's thesis made literal. The panel is a d3→d2 gradient; the water lives in a fixed 132px `.gauge` between the list and the capacity readout, translated — never scaled — to the level, so the waterline is exactly 1px at any fill and crosses no text. Every ink inside `.wall__list` is --ink or --ink-dim: --ink-faint measures 4.30:1 on a hovered row and 3.97:1 on a selected one.

components.name: Capacity Gauge
components.description: The water's whole world. Its height IS total capacity, so --used and --pending resolve against it. overflow:hidden lets the water be translated rather than scaled without escaping the band. Nothing inside it is text, which is the point: the waterline can never cross a row again. Measured 10.6 / 46.2 / 116.2 / 132px at 8 / 35 / 88 / 100%.

components.name: Selection Bar
components.description: Appears above the wall's list when anything is ticked. Opaque --d3, because the destructive control lives here and its ratio must be a property of this rule rather than of whatever veil a row is wearing. The readout takes its own line: the wall is 300px and the count is three clauses long. Stub sizes are skipped rather than added as zeros — the watch never reported one.
components.html: 3 selected · 41.2 MB (2 files) · 1 unreadable, size unknown

components.name: Delete Confirmation
components.description: Inline, above the list, never a modal — 'Never Cover The Number' forbids anything floating over the capacity readout, and the free-space figure is what someone deciding whether to delete wants in view. Opaque --notice-ground: --alert 4.77:1, --ink-dim 6.02:1, --ink 14.14:1. Focus lands on 'Keep them'; Escape cancels and returns focus to the Delete button. The body is the part that scrolls in a short window, so the two buttons are never below the fold. Three copies, because a broken stub is not a file and a journal row with nothing behind it is not a deletion at all.

components.name: Danger Button
components.description: Two rules. It never lives in a row — only on an opaque ground, so its contrast is a property of its own rule (--d3 5.08:1, --notice-ground 4.77:1; a selected row is 3.80:1 and a hovered one 4.12:1). And it never tints its own ground — an alert-hued 10% wash drops those to 4.60 and 4.28, so hover moves the border to --ink-dim (6.41:1 / 6.02:1) instead. The word carries the meaning, so 'colour never signals alone' holds without a fill.

components.name: Arrangement Chip
components.description: A segmented view toggle over a set that does not change: same files, differently ordered. Distinct from the rail's .nav on purpose — the rail switches WHAT the library shows you and is navigation; this switches HOW one fixed list is arranged. State lives in aria-pressed, not in a class. Files is the default and stays the default: it is the order list_dir('Music') returned, and the panel opens on the device's answer rather than on Pelican's memory of it. --ink-dim on --d3 6.41:1; pressed, --ink on the #1b2733 composite 12.51:1; --edge border 3.40 / 3.27.

narrative.overview:
Pelican is a cold blue-black room with one absolute horizontal in it. The ground (`#070c13`) is fjord water seen from above; every surface in the app sits at a stated depth in that water, and depth is the only spatial idea the system has. Above the waterline is `--air` — the library, where you browse your own music. The water itself is confined to a fixed 132px gauge between the watch's track list and its capacity readout, whose height *is* total capacity; it is no longer a fill behind the whole panel, because at any level below 100% its 1px line and its bloom cut horizontally through the track rows. Below it are `--d1` through `--d4`, each colder, darker and denser than the last, ending at the player bar, which is the deepest surface on screen. One warm value, brass (`#d8963f`), is the low sun on the water; it appears on the active state and the primary action and nowhere else.

The register is Scandinavian restraint: the craft lives in the joinery — a 1px waterline with a bloom that falls only downward, a hairline that is 5.8% ink and not a border-coloured line, a scrollbar drawn rather than inherited — and there is no applied ornament anywhere. Nothing is decorated to look designed. The density is a desktop utility's: 13px body, 46px titlebar, 66px player, rows at 7px vertical padding. It reads like a native Mac tool because it is built out of the same materials one is: the system type stack, no bundled asset, no raster of any kind.

The product's promises are load-bearing on the visuals. Nothing leaves the machine, which means no webfont, no remote image, no telemetry pixel; the frontend is vanilla HTML/CSS/JS with no framework and no bundler, so the system has to be expressible in one 494-line stylesheet and custom properties on `:root`. And the app ships zero rasters: album art is a code-drawn frame; this build never fills it — `read_fast` passes `read_cover_art(false)` and nothing in the frontend sets a background on `.cover`. The measured comp spec records 10 regions and 0 plates.
keyCharacteristics: Depth as the only spatial metaphor; five named grounds, no shadow ladder.
One absolute horizontal — the waterline — as the only structural rule, with a stated range: it travels within the gauge and never crosses type.
Exactly one warm value, reserved; everything else is blue-black and ink.
Colour never signals alone; every state also says its name in words.
No shipped rasters, no bundled fonts, no icon font: SVG paths and CSS.
Container queries, not media queries — this is a window, not a viewport.
One thing moves with intent (the water); nothing loops or pulses at rest.
Two navigation vocabularies, deliberately distinct: `.nav` in the rail switches what the library shows you; `.chip` in the wall switches how one fixed list is arranged.

rules.name: The One Warm Value Rule
rules.body: Brass marks the active state and the primary action. It is never a hover colour, never a heading colour, never a border on something inert. If a second thing on screen wants to be brass, one of them is not actually the primary action.

rules.name: The Word With The Colour Rule
rules.body: No state is carried by hue alone. Red appears only alongside its sentence; the connection dot only alongside the word `connected` or `no watch found`; over-capacity turns red *and* changes its text to `… too much`. Test: convert the screen to greyscale — if a state became unreadable, the state is under-built.

rules.name: The Ground You Actually Sit On Rule
rules.body: A contrast ratio is measured against the composite an element renders over, not against the token named in its parent's rule. Three failures in this build came from measuring against the wrong ground: `--alert` inside `.notice` inside a translucent `.transfer` read 5.06:1 on paper and 4.18:1 on the real three-layer composite; `--ink-faint` in the rail read 5.28:1 on `--air` and 4.09:1 on `--surface-2` over the rail gradient; the capacity readout read fine until `.water`'s `--d1` stop rose behind it at 4.18:1. Where a stack cannot be pinned down — the transfer card floats over scrolling album art — give the element an opaque ground and the question stops being open.

rules.name: The Deeper Is Colder Rule
rules.body: A surface's colour states its depth. Moving a panel down the ladder means moving it toward `#060e17`; there is no lighter- means-nearer inversion anywhere in the system.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: There is no display face and no mono face. Hierarchy is made from weight (400 / 590 / 640 / 660), size, and ink tier — never from a second family. A bundled webfont is a network promise this product does not make.

rules.name: The Tabular Number Rule
rules.body: Any numeral a user might compare against another numeral carries `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`. In practice that is every number in the app.

rules.name: The Measure Rule
rules.body: Prose blocks are capped at 34ch (album credits, the disconnected explanation). Nothing in this app is long-form; if a string needs more than 34 characters of width, it is data, not prose.

rules.name: The Window Not Viewport Rule
rules.body: Every breakpoint in this system is `@container shell (max-width: …)`. Adding a `@media (max-width: …)` layout rule is a defect: it makes the app answer to the display instead of to itself.

rules.name: The Nothing Unreachable Rule
rules.body: No breakpoint may remove a navigation target. Panels may re-flow, re-orient or scroll; they may not disappear with their contents. Content that is duplicated elsewhere (the rail's playlist note) may be dropped; content that is unique may not.

rules.name: The Tonal Depth Rule
rules.body: New surfaces take a depth from the ladder; they do not take a shadow. If a panel needs to read as further away, it moves toward `#060e17`, not under a blur.

rules.name: The One Luminous Object Rule
rules.body: The waterline is the only thing in the app that emits light, and it lights downward only. No second glow, no accent bloom, no brass halo, and no light cast up into the air where text lives.

rules.name: The Floor Under The Glass Rule
rules.body: A translucent surface that can float over arbitrary content gets an opaque or near-opaque base beneath its blur. Glass is a look, not a contrast strategy; without a floor, every ink on the panel inherits its ratio from whatever scrolls behind it.

rules.name: The Never Cover The Number Rule
rules.body: Floating surfaces are docked with explicit insets that clear the capacity readout. A transient panel may cover the library; it may never cover the fact that is changing.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Structural separation is a 5.8%-ink 1px line. Not a grey, not a `--border` colour, not a 2px rule, and never two lines where the tonal step already separates the panels.

rules.name: The Scale Has A Floor Rule
rules.body: 6 / 10 / 14 governs anything with an interior. An element smaller than about 16px in its short dimension takes a radius from its own geometry instead, and that exception is registered rather than assumed. Adding a fifth off-scale radius means registering it too, or it is drift.

rules.name: The No Applied Ornament Rule
rules.body: No borders that do not separate, no gradients that do not describe depth, no rounded corner larger than 14px, no decorative divider. If a shape is not doing structural work, remove it.

dos: Do place a new surface on the depth ladder (`--air`, `--air-2`, `--d1`–`--d4`) and let its colour state how deep it is.
Do use the two white veils (4.8% / 7.8%) for raised and current states, and the two hairlines (5.8% structural / 10.5% control) for edges.
Do pair every colour-carried state with its word, and check the screen in greyscale before calling it done.
Do keep `--ink-faint` at `#7d8c9b`; the 5.28:1 ratio is the reason it is that value.
Do write new breakpoints as `@container shell (max-width: …)`.
Do draw new icons as inline SVG paths in the sprite, `fill/stroke: currentColor` at 15×14 (17×16 large), stroke-width 1.4, round caps.
Do keep prose blocks at or under 34ch.
Do register an off-scale radius in `.impeccable/config.json` when an element is too small for the 6/10/14 scale, rather than letting it pass unremarked.
Do animate colour and background at 120ms, state arrivals at 260ms, and reserve 900ms for the water alone.
donts: Don't put brass on anything that is not the primary action or the active state — not on hover, not on a heading, not on a border.
Don't add a drop shadow to convey elevation; the cover lift is the only one, and depth is tonal.
Don't introduce a second font family, a webfont, or an icon font. The no-network promise and the auditable dependency surface both depend on it.
Don't ship a raster. Album art is a code-drawn frame filled from the user's own files at runtime; the build records 0 plates and should stay there.

Don't make the pending band a child of `.water`: its percentage height resolves against the water's own height, so the band shrinks as the watch empties. It is a fraction of total capacity, so it measures against the wall.

Don't animate `.water` by scaling or by compressing the gradient into a short box. It is full-height and translated; that is what keeps the waterline exactly 1px and the depth ramp truthful at low levels.
Don't claim a contrast ratio against a parent's declared colour when the element renders over a composite. Measure the stack, or make the ground opaque.
Don't put a translucent surface over content you do not control without a floor under the blur.
Don't use `pointer-events: none` to disable a control; opacity plus a stated reason.
Don't let a floating panel cover the capacity readout.
Don't remove a navigation target at a breakpoint. Re-flow it.
Don't invent placeholder numbers. Capacities, counts, sizes and formats are read from the device and the user's files; a fabricated value in this app is a lie about their hardware.
Don't add anything that loops, pulses or breathes at rest.
